notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2025'). Nu reports under IFRS in US dollars, in thousands; values are converted to billions. Source is the FY2025 Form 20-F (filed April 8, 2026, accession 0001292814-26-002166). SEC companyfacts has no FY2025 facts for Nu, so no xbrl objects are recorded. LEADER: the 20-F's Item 7.A table (as of March 1, 2026) gives Vélez's holding by class (0.1% of Class A, 88.3% of Class B) and his voting power (74.4%) but not a percentage of all shares, so pctEconomic is null and leader.derived gives 18.64% from the stated counts, for an editor to approve. His figure includes 1,500,000 Class B shares held by his wife and the shares of Rua California Ltd., which the 20-F also lists separately as a 5% holder; Rua California is not added as a holder because it is inside his figure. HOLDERS: largestHolders is null. The other 5% holders are given only as percentages of Class A, not of all shares, and are not converted here: BlackRock 266,236,594 Class A (6.9%, 13G filed November 8, 2024) and Baillie Gifford & Co 265,160,474 (6.9%, 13G filed April 30, 2025); Sequoia and Capital Research no longer appear. Co-founder Cristina Junqueira holds 11,427,060 Class A (0.3%) and 119,476,200 Class B (11.7%), 9.9% of votes. STOCK COMP: 0.33 is Nu's 'Total share-based compensation expenses' for 2025 ($329.5 million). It includes related corporate and social security taxes and a $29.5 million hedge fair-value adjustment. The cash-flow add-back for share-based payments is $271.8 million. GEOGRAPHY: the geographic table totals $12.08 billion, below the $15.77 billion total revenue in the income statement, because it covers only the revenue types listed in its footnote; the 20-F does not reconcile the two totals. It now groups everything outside Brazil and Mexico as 'Other countries'. BUYBACKS: none in 2025; the financing section has no repurchase line. Nu began repurchasing Class A shares in 2026 (40,659,600 shares by September 30, 2026, per its Q3 2026 interim statements). PLAN: none described in the sections read.

ecosystem.notes: Total revenue is mostly interest income on credit cards and loans, not fees on purchase volume, so Revenue / PV is not Nubank's take on card spending. The revenue directly tied to PV is card income: the 20-F says "For the year ended December 31, 2025, total credit and prepaid cards income was US$1,720.3 million, equivalent to 1.2% of PV" (the sentence then says "over the year ended December 31, 2024", which appears to be a drafting slip). PV covers credit and prepaid cards only and excludes Pix.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Nubank revenue is mostly interest income; only interchange fees relate to purchase volume.

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Taxes: no FY2025 facts in companyfacts; value from the cash-flow statement, USD 1,641,663 thousand. R&D not reported as a separate line, so rnd is null.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 20-F). Judgement: bank rule, not the payments formula. Nu is a deposit-funded lender: its operating cash flow is dominated by growth in credit-card receivables and loans (−22.75bn) and deposits (+12.86bn), not by collecting revenue, which is the condition that makes the formula meaningless for banks. So paidOut is null (comparable: false) and altPaidOut = noninterest expense − D&A − SBC + income taxes paid. Noninterest expense = transactional expenses (366,183) + total operating (expenses) income (2,752,894, net of 130,090 other income), from the income statement; expected credit loss (4,204,876) is a provision and interest and other financial expenses (4,578,680) are interest, both excluded as at BofA. D&A, SBC and taxes paid come from the cash-flow statement. Interest paid in cash (92,292) is far below interest expense (4,578,680); the cash-flow statement does not explain the gap, so it is recorded as stated. No xbrl objects: companyfacts has no FY2025 facts for Nu. All figures US$ thousands. Reports in USD.
